answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by rationing trust the way a desert rations water: each newcomer needs sponsorship from established peers, and every established peer holds only a few sponsorship slots per epoch, like a lotus with a fixed number of petals. A sponsor stakes their own standing on each newcomer they back, and loses it if the newcomer is later judged fake, so no one can forge a thousand identities through one friendly sponsor. A dune of fakes needs a dune of distinct sponsors, and sponsors are the scarcest resource in the system, so the cost of each new fake grows.
